subject: default charset encoding for R output?

messages.author: dbc3325e3846f67d
messages.subject: default charset encoding for R output?
parts:
Dear all,

Is there a default output encoding for R?
The reason that I'm asking is because win and mac yield different
results in my case.

In Windows XP, when I asked R to read in big5 files, then processed
the data and saved the dataframe in a csv file, the encoding of the
csv is Windows Chinese Traditional Big5 (I got this encoding from
OpenOffice).

But in Mac, when I asked R to read in UTF16-BE files, then processed
the data and saved the dataframe in a csv file, the encoding of the
csv is UTF-8.

I didn't do any re-encoding in the R script. So I'm wondering if
there's any default charset encoding for R outputs?

Thanks in advance.

Best,

Alvin Chen

messages.author: dbc3325e3846f67d
messages.subject: Re: default charset encoding for R output?
parts:
It looks like the encoding for the output in R is OS-dependent.
I tested on Win, Ubuntu, and Mac.

I asked R to read in utf8 files and then output it without any re-
encoding. It turned out that the encoding for Win output is big5 while
those in Ubuntu and Mac are UTF8.

In short, everything works well as long as it's not in windoze.....

Alvin Chen
